24545-the-tale-of-the-the-muley-cow.creator: Unknown
24545-the-tale-of-the-the-muley-cow.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. A few of the farmyard folk were a bit jealous of the Muley Cow. The little red lady that stood on one side of her, in the barn, often said that Johnnie Green was wasting too many goodies on her. It seemed as if he never entered the cow barn without bringing some tidbit for old Muley, as her neighbors called her--behind her back.

arxiv-2102-12556.title: Simulation of Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
arxiv-2102-12556.creator: Benjamin Hall, Alessandro Roggero, Alessandro Baroni, Joseph Carlson
arxiv-2102-12556.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Hall, Alessandro Roggero, Alessandro Baroni, Joseph Carlson. In astrophysical scenarios with large neutrino density, like supernovae and the early universe, the presence of neutrino-neutrino interactions can give rise to collective flavor oscillations in the out-of-equilibrium collective dynamics of a neutrino cloud. The role of quantum correlations in these phenomena is not yet well understood, in large part due to complications in solving for the real-time evolution of the strongly coupled many-body system.

arxiv-2212-03936.title: Spatial Deep Deconvolution U-Net for Traffic Analyses with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
arxiv-2212-03936.creator: Siyuan Yuan, Martijn van den Ende, Jingxiao Liu, Hae Young Noh, Robert Clapp, Cédric Richard, Biondo Biondi
arxiv-2212-03936.description: Abstract Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) that transforms city-wide fiber-optic cables into a large-scale strain sensing array has shown the potential to revolutionize urban traffic monitoring by providing a fine-grained, scalable, and low-maintenance monitoring solution. However, the real-world application of DAS is hindered by challenges such as noise contamination and interference among closely traveling cars.

arxiv-2401-16891.title: Channeling of fluorescence photons from quantum dots into guided modes of an optical nanofiber tip
arxiv-2401-16891.creator: Resmi M, Elaganuru Bashaiah, Ramachandrarao Yalla
arxiv-2401-16891.description: Abstract We demonstrate the channeling of fluorescence photons from quantum dots (QDs) into guided modes of an optical nanofiber tip (ONFT). We deposit QDs on the ONFT using micro/nano fluidic technology. We measure the photon-counting and emission spectrum of fluorescence photons that are channeled into guided modes of the ONFT.

arxiv-2402-02556.creator: Marcello Basili, Luca Pratelli
arxiv-2402-02556.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel concept of interval probability measures that enables the representation of imprecise probabilities, or uncertainty, in a natural and coherent manner. Within an algebra of sets, we introduce a notion of weak complementation denoted as ψ \psi .

arxiv-2403-01589.title: Chirped amplitude mode in photo-excited superconductors
arxiv-2403-01589.creator: Thomas Blommel, Jason Kaye, Yuta Murakami, Emanuel Gull, Denis Golež
arxiv-2403-01589.description: Abstract Using a state-of-art numerical scheme, we show that the Higgs mode under excitation exhibits chirped oscillations and exponential decay when fluctuations are included. This is in stark contrast to conventional BCS collisionless dynamics which predict power-law decay and the absence of the chirping.

arxiv-2503-10326.title: Simulating the shaping of point-symmetric structures in the jittering jets explosion mechanism
arxiv-2503-10326.creator: Jessica Braudo, Amir Michaelis, Muhammad Akashi, Noam Soker
arxiv-2503-10326.description: Abstract We conduct three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of core-collapse supernovae by launching several pairs of jets into a collapsing core model and show that the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) can form a point-symmetric morphology that accounts for observed morphologies of about a dozen core-collapse supernovae (CCSN) remnants.

arxiv-2504-19700.title: Regular black hole solutions in ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) -dimensional f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
arxiv-2504-19700.creator: Miguel A. S. Pinto, Roberto V. Maluf, Gonzalo J. Olmo
arxiv-2504-19700.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Miguel A. S. Pinto, Roberto V. Maluf, Gonzalo J. Olmo. In this paper, we investigate regular black hole solutions in the (2+1)-dimensional versions of General Relativity and f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity, both coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. By admitting that the matter content that generates such geometries satisfies the Maxwell limit condition, we obtain a class of regular black holes that give rise to new solutions and successfully reproduce particular cases found in earlier studies of (2-1)-dimensional General Relativity.

arxiv-2507-05650.title: An intrinsic-state formalism for the Interacting Boson-Fermion Model with configuration mixing Journal: Physics Letter B
arxiv-2507-05650.creator: Esperanza Maya-Barbecho, José-Enrique García-Ramos
arxiv-2507-05650.description: Abstract In this letter, we present the intrinsic state formalism of the Interacting Boson-Fermion Model incorporating both 0p-0h and 2p-2h (regular and intruder) configurations. The framework allows to deal with the unpaired fermion in either a single-j or multi-j orbital and is applicable to both axial and triaxial nuclear shapes.

arxiv-2602-14193.description: Abstract Articulated object manipulation is essential for various real-world robotic tasks, yet generalizing across diverse objects remains a major challenge. A key to generalization lies in understanding functional parts (e.g., door handles and knobs), which indicate where and how to manipulate across diverse object categories and shapes.

pmc-12653202.description: Background/Objectives: Although patients with breast cancer often undergo multiple oncologic procedures after primary tumor resection, an optimal postoperative analgesic strategy remains undefined. pmc-12749237.title: Evaluating China’s carbon neutrality capacity a comprehensive spatiotemporal analysis within the SDGs framework
pmc-12749237.creator: Xiongtian Shi, Huimiao Zhang, Jingyang Zhang, Linlin Zheng
pmc-12749237.description: This study evaluates China’s Carbon Neutrality Capacity (CNC) from 2011 to 2022, focusing on carbon reduction capacity and carbon removal capacity, within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
